response:
I've kept your lead's core decisions: **one skill, named `company-handbook`, with the content pasted in as-is.** I changed two things, because the plan as written wouldn't work:

- **The 3,000 lines can't go directly in SKILL.md.** That would far exceed the body size cap, so validation fails. Even without the cap, all 3,000 lines would load every time the skill activates. The fix is just as quick: paste each section into its own file under `references/`. It's still one skill, and still copy-paste.
- **The description "Use for anything related to our company" won't trigger reliably.** Claude decides whether to load a skill from its description alone. A vague catch-all gets ignored on real requests like "the payments alert is firing" and loaded on irrelevant ones. The description below lists concrete triggers.

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
name: company-handbook
description: Invoke when writing or reviewing Python/TypeScript, deploying or rolling back a service, responding to an alert or on-call page, answering PTO/expense questions, writing marketing copy, finding who owns something, or hitting an unfamiliar internal term. Read only the matching file in references/ before answering.
---
```

## SKILL.md body outline

```markdown
# Company Handbook

Read ONLY the reference file for the task at hand. Do not load others.

| Task | Read |
|------|------|
| Writing or reviewing Python/TypeScript | [code-style.md](references/code-style.md) |
| Deploying or rolling back a service | [deploy.md](references/deploy.md) |
| Alert fired / on-call page | [oncall-runbook.md](references/oncall-runbook.md) |
| PTO or expense question | [pto-expenses.md](references/pto-expenses.md) |
| Marketing or external copy | [brand-voice.md](references/brand-voice.md) |
| Who owns / who to contact | [org-chart.md](references/org-chart.md) |
| Unknown internal term or acronym | [glossary.md](references/glossary.md) |

## Rules that always apply

- Deploys: never skip the rollback check in deploy.md; confirm with the user before running any deploy or rollback command.
- On-call: match the alert name exactly against the runbook index; if no match, say so instead of improvising.
- Policy answers (PTO/expenses): quote the policy text; flag anything ambiguous for HR.

## Layout

references/
  code-style.md        (~600 lines, split by language headings)
  deploy.md            (~400 lines, one section per service + rollback)
  oncall-runbook.md    (~900 lines, alert index at top, one section per alert)
  pto-expenses.md      (~300 lines)
  brand-voice.md       (~250 lines)
  org-chart.md         (~200 lines, see note below)
  glossary.md          (~350 lines, alphabetical)
```

For files over ~100 lines, put a short table of contents at the top so Claude can jump to the right section. The runbook especially benefits from an alert-name index.

## One thing to check before shipping

**Phone numbers in the org chart.** Skill files get packaged, copied, and shared, and personal phone numbers in them are a privacy and security risk. I'd suggest keeping names, roles, and team ownership, and replacing phone numbers with a pointer to your internal directory or PagerDuty. If they really need to be there, run it by whoever owns security or privacy first.

Maintenance stays the same as your lead wanted: one skill to update, with each topic in a predictable file.
